the more service workers must engage in dealing with complaining customers and the more they suppress emotion while doing so, the more they are likely to experience depression symptoms.
engaging with complaints and suppressing emotions at work is associated with experience of depression and/or anxiety symptoms.
the job characteristics of "Engage with Complaints" and "Suppressing Emotions" are significantly related to the experience of mental health problems in Korean customer service workers.

the relationship between work related stressors and depression and anxiety symptoms in customer service workers.
the importance of mental health promotion at work for service workers who are exposed to the emotional labor.
the mental health of customer service workers and the need to improve their work environment and work conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
suppressing emotion and engaging in complaining customers at work are related to the experience of mental health problems.
the experience of depression and symptoms of anxiety is associated with the job characteristics of engaging with complaining customers and suppression of emotions.
suppressing emotion and engaging more with complaining customers at the workplace are related to the experience of depression and/or anxiety symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more workers engage with complaining customers the more they suppress emotion at work and the more they experience depression and anxiety.
the more service workers are required to engage with complaining customers, the more they must suppress their emotions.
the more service workers must engage and suppress at work, the more likely they will experience depression and anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to develop a work environment that can reduce the mental health burden on service workers by providing support for dealing with complaining customers and reducing emotional suppression at work.
service workers who engage with complaints and suppressing emotion at a high level are more likely to experience mental health problems.

service workers should be protected from mental health problems by minimizing the need to engage with complaining customers at the workplace and by providing support to help service workers to suppress emotion.
